ReSolveHPLC mobile-phase reuse
ReSolve for Quality Control

Reduce QC operating costs and increase laboratory capacity without compromising analytical reliability.

ReSolve intelligently recycles uncontaminated mobile phase, between peaks, in isocratic HPLC methods.

  • Lab efficiency
  • Reduced handling
  • Lower operating cost
  • Analytical confidence

Reduce routine mobile-phase preparation, chemical handling and fresh-solvent demand in isocratic workflows. ReSolve can release analyst time for higher-value QC work while method-specific evidence and controls support analytical confidence.

For isocratic HPLC methods only. Not for gradient methods.

See how ReSolve works

One flow. Two destinations.

  1. The detector monitors the signal during an isocratic run.
  2. Detected peak fractions are directed to waste.
  3. Suitable mobile phase between peaks is routed back for reuse.

Routing settings and method suitability must be confirmed for the proposed workflow.

Analytical performance comes first

The PMBrc / SETU chromatographic study compared fresh and recovered mobile phase in two matched 96-injection sequences and reported comparable chromatography for the evaluated method.

This method-specific result does not establish performance or savings for other workflows.

12 method-specific analytical checks

Use these criteria to assess whether mobile-phase reuse affects the analytical performance of a specific QC method.

  • Retention time
  • Peak area / assay
  • Resolution
  • Tailing factor
  • Theoretical plates
  • Relative retention
  • Impurity levels
  • Baseline noise / drift
  • Blank response
  • Repeatability
  • System suitability
  • Mobile-phase performance / suitability

Your QC questions

Will reused mobile phase affect our results?

Suitability depends on the method and operating conditions. The published comparison is useful supporting evidence; your QC and QA requirements determine the checks needed for your own use.

Does ReSolve work with gradient methods?

No. ReSolve is intended for isocratic HPLC methods. Method suitability must be confirmed for each proposed workflow.

Does released analyst time count as a cash saving?

It creates potential capacity for other work. It is a cash saving only where an actual expense falls; the published routing percentage does not demonstrate a time saving.

Your QA questions

Keeping resources in use

Circular use within your laboratory

Flow between peaks returns to the reservoir; detected peak fractions go to waste. ReSolve reuses suitable prepared mobile phase within the workflow—it does not purify collected waste solvent.

Where your laboratory could benefit

Resource efficiency

Keep suitable mobile phase in use for longer and assess the resulting change in fresh-phase consumption.

Waste prevention

Prevent suitable flow from going straight to waste. Net waste reduction depends on your actual preparation, use and disposal practices.

Solvent handling

Lower consumption and waste may reduce container movements and handling. Any change in exposure or safety risk needs your EHS team’s assessment.

Continuous measurement.
Sustained sustainability.

Make sustainability an ongoing operating metric

ReSolve continuously records mobile phase routed for reuse and to waste, creating a sustained measure of solvent-use efficiency over time rather than a one-off sustainability project.

Combine these records with fresh-solvent consumption and waste-disposal data to track verified laboratory impact over time. Carbon and transport benefits should only be reported where supported by measured activity and documented emissions factors.

Your sustainability questions

Does 94.5% reuse mean 94.5% less hazardous waste?

No. The study figure describes routing in its evaluated method. Your net solvent and waste reductions require comparison with your own consumption and disposal baseline.

Can we include CO₂e benefits?

Where supported by measured activity and appropriate emissions factors. Potential benefits may arise from solvent production, waste treatment and transport changes. Include additional device impacts and avoid counting transport twice.

Will deliveries and waste collections fall?

Only if reduced consumption changes actual ordering and collection activity. Lower litres alone do not demonstrate fewer journeys.

Measure the sustainability opportunity

Use your laboratory baseline to assess fresh-solvent reduction, hazardous-waste prevention and the measures you can report over time.

Focus on the costs that can actually change

Solvent cost reduction

Value reductions in fresh-solvent consumption using your actual blended mobile-phase cost.

Disposal cost reduction

Apply your contracted disposal charges to net waste reductions. Separate variable charges from fixed collection or minimum fees.

Commercial fit

Assess eligible usage, expected solvent and variable waste-disposal savings, implementation scope and supplier support as part of the purchase decision.

Your purchasing questions

How should we assess the commercial case?

Use your site’s eligible solvent consumption, blended solvent cost and variable waste-disposal charges. Keep redeployed analyst hours separate from direct cash savings.

Can this fit our existing HPLC equipment?

Yes. ReSolve is designed to work with all HPLC systems and detectors. Method suitability should be confirmed for the proposed workflow.

Can we compare several instruments or sites?

Yes, using consistent assumptions and local usage, costs and technical requirements. Assess each laboratory’s suitable methods rather than applying a single published reuse rate across all instruments.

Research & evidence

Measured evidence, clearly separated from site-specific claims

Start with the PMBrc / SETU chromatographic study, then review the separate 98-injection routing record. Measured findings are kept distinct from benefits that require your own site baseline.

01 · PMBrc / SETU study

Fresh versus recovered mobile phase

The Pharmaceutical & Molecular Biotechnology Research Centre at South East Technological University compared two matched 96-injection sequences for a selected isocratic paracetamol and ibuprofen method.

96 + 96injections in two matched sequences
94.5%mobile phase routed for reuse in the evaluated method
Comparablechromatography reported for this method
Selected chromatography results
QC measureFresh phaseRecovered phaseReported difference
Paracetamol retention time1.21 ± 0.00 min1.21 ± 0.00 min0.00%
Ibuprofen retention time5.65 ± 0.01 min5.67 ± 0.01 min+0.35%
Paracetamol peak area1670.9 ± 4.7 mAU·s1673.1 ± 5.2 mAU·s+0.1%
Peak resolution (EP)30.31 ± 0.0430.27 ± 0.05-0.13%

The study reported no observed difference in baseline noise/stability and no detectable paracetamol or ibuprofen in recovered phase by LC/MS. These are findings for the evaluated method, not acceptance criteria for another laboratory.

02 · Recorded routing evidence

Recorded routing evidence

One 98-injection isocratic sequence recorded 1,111.004 mL routed for reuse and 63.533 mL directed to waste — 94.59% routed for reuse in that sequence.

What it does — and does not — show

It demonstrates measured routing performance. It does not by itself establish chromatographic equivalence, net site solvent savings, waste reduction or lifecycle emissions.

Evidence answers “can it work?” Your site assessment answers “will it work here?” Use the published study and routing record to define what must be demonstrated for your own methods.
From evidence to site decision

What your laboratory still needs to establish

The published and recorded evidence supports evaluation. Your site still determines whether ReSolve is suitable for the specific method, system and controlled workflow.

  • Qualification, change control, SOPs and training requirements
  • Actual net reduction in fresh mobile-phase purchasing
  • Actual reduction in hazardous waste sent for disposal
  • Site economics and any carbon claim using your own baseline and approved factors

Additional benefits to assess at your site

  • Waste disposal: potential savings depend on actual waste reduction and disposal charges.
  • Analyst time: less preparation and handling may free time for other work.
  • CO₂: potential reductions from fewer solvent deliveries and less hazardous HPLC waste sent for disposal, subject to actual changes in transport and waste treatment.

Assess these during the site review; they are not included in the calculated saving.

How the calculation works

Annual usage: systems × flow (mL/min) × 60 × hours/day × days/week × weeks/year ÷ 1,000. Monthly usage = annual usage ÷ 12.

Annual mobile-phase saving: annual usage × estimated net reduction × cost per litre.

Disposal, analyst time and CO₂ benefits are not included. Equipment and implementation costs are not deducted.
